In 1945, at the end of World War II, Germany has capitulated as soon as the Soviet army crossed its border. This led to a separation of the post-war world into two powerful alliances of states - the North Atlantic Confederation and the Great Asian Alliance. The economic disparity and arms race have made a full-scale war between the two sides an inevitability.

![](https://i.ibb.co/WWtrBvgS/aow1.png)
N.A.C. and G.A.A.
The war between two alliances has ended in a decisive victory of the North-Atlantic Confederation. This success allowed it to reinforce its position as the world hegemon, and soon all other countries of the world joined the alliance, including those from the defeated Great Asian Alliance. The Global Confederation was formed, governed by the Senate, where all member nations' representatives were gathered.

During the first years of its world domination, humanity looked into the future with optimism. The economy, which no longer had to support the military industrial complex, has reorganized towards scientific and technical progress. Thanks to the Confederation policies, great breakthroughs were achieved in all fields of science and medicine.

![](https://i.ibb.co/b5x8xDcv/w-04-1.jpg)

Twenty years have passed. Although wars over resources became a thing of the past, the problem of economic inequality between the rich and the poor has remained unsolved. In many regions of the world grew resentment towards the policy of the Senate. With time, the situation only became worse. The discontented united into underground movements, armed by sympathizer countries. Old military factories began operating again, producing vehicles and equipment for the rebels.

In 2038, the first uprising starts in Peru. The Confederation Senate has sent peacekeeping forces to stabilize the region, which at first have succeeded in restoring order in the country. However, despite their failure, the rebels have merely retreated to the jungle. They recovered their strength and attacked again. Thanks to tactical brilliance of general Monteros, the Peru Liberation Army managed to defeat the peacekeeping corps of the Confedereation. This victory sparked armed uprisings around the entire globe.

![](https://i.ibb.co/Ng4X5wXd/12-1.png)

## The Confederation in 2040

> The world is on fire, and we are in the thick of it! Every minute, from all corners of the world, come reports of new outbreaks of rebellion. The rebels have demanded that the Senate be dissolved and the Old World Order be restored. But we do not intend to make concessions. The rebellion must be suppressed by any means!..

![](https://i.ibb.co/gMGQZW4s/senate.jpg)
The Confederation Senate
The Global Confederation's ideology can be described as: "Peace in the name of progress, progress in the name of peace". And in twenty years of its rule, humanity really did achieve significant progress in many fields of science. Many diseases were permanently vanquished, the planet's ecology was improved, and beautiful, bright cities were built for its inhabitants.

But these successes did not come for free. The Senate's good intentions do not always equally consider the interests of all member nations of the alliance. Because of this the government struggles with discontent. The prosperity of some comes at the cost of others, less fortunate - they are the ones who usually voice their grievances.

In 2040 this discontent develops into open conflict. Disjointed at first, the uprisings soon unite under the common banner of the Resistance. The Senate is forced to allocate significant resources on expansion of the army and suppression of revolts across the globe.

![](https://i.ibb.co/bM99dxT7/conf-a-1.jpg)

## The Confederation Military

> We were preparing to suppress the uprising, but we did not expect the rebels to begin such a large-scale war so soon...

![](https://i.ibb.co/Rpyx22G9/11.jpg)

The Confederation military has been significantly reduced over the twenty years of peace. However, the peacekeeping corps, which has become the core of the new Confederation Army, is armed with the most advanced vehicles and equipment.

The military doctrine of the Confederation is based on its technological superiority. Its bases are dispersed to effectively defend important strategic points. For offensive operations, its commanders prefer to rely on force concentration, assembling large strike groups of heavy equipment.

In the air, the faction relies on the speed of its modern jet fighters and bombers. Helicopters with advanced scanners fulfill the scouting role.

The backbone of the Confederation Navy is large surface vessels. Together with "Delta"-class assault vehicles the Confederation Navy is perfectly suited to support land operations.

![](https://i.ibb.co/6jrJkS0/wings-render-polishing-final-pravki.jpg)

## The Space Program

> The Command has declared a red danger level. The Senate supports the use of a Space Strike to prevent a nuclear threat. This will be the first combat use of the new weapon. Construction of a prototype Space System has begun. After this, the advantage will be on our side.

![](https://i.ibb.co/Ldw5QfGL/Third-ion-cannon.webp)

This top secret initiative deserves a special mention. It implies launching a network of satellites armed with orbital beam weapons, able to strike anywhere on the planet. A large number of facilities and labs have been constructed for the program, including centers in USA and Canada.

Despite the direct interference from the Resistance, the Confederation was able to complete the construction of the satellites network. Due to the escalation of the global conflict, the Senate has made the decision to allow deployment of this new weapon in ongoing battles.

![](https://i.ibb.co/SDGrmwTy/w-08.jpg)

## The Resistance in 2040

> Today, we have challenged the system! Organized uprisings have sparked the whole world with the fire of hope! Hopes are for the overthrow of the Confederation's regime. Hidden too long in the shadows, we have suffered privation, gathered strength, and prepared for this day.

![](https://i.ibb.co/FLVH1zC3/Blitz-convoy-render-polishing-f1.jpg)

In 2040, the Resistance grows from the local rebellion in Peru into a global organization with numerous contacts in different countries, able to challenge even the Global Confederation.

The Resistance is united by the common goal of liberating the nations of the world from the yoke of the Confederation and creating a new, more just world order. However, it is currently hard to say what exactly this new world would look like.

There are Resistance sympathizers even inside the Global Confederation itself. Thanks to them, the Resistance regularly receives confidential information. A wide network of agents and spies ensures that no decision of the Senate would become a surprise for the Resistance.

Due to the unequal strengths, the Resistance is ready to resort to large-scale terror in the name of liberation, including using nuclear weapons.

![](https://i.ibb.co/qF3w54Ty/sopr-a-1.jpg)

## The Resistance Military

> Fight for freedom, brothers! Fight shoulder to shoulder! Our strength is unity! You will be led by experienced commanders, hardened in the Peruvian conflict. Follow their orders, and victory will be ours!

![](https://i.ibb.co/gFD8J93v/w-03.jpg)

The Resistance includes armed militias from across the globe, united in their desire to overthrow the Senate's rule. The Confederation is a difficult enemy, especially if it will be able to reconfigure its economy into war economy. The Resistance is lagging behind in technological advancement and has access to a limited amount of advanced vehicles and equipment, relying on old blueprints, "lost" and "retired" vehicles of the Confederation, or local manufacturing.

All of this forces the Resistance commanders to adapt their military doctrine. They rely on speed and maneuverability of their units, striking the enemy's vulnerable points and forcing fights in favorable conditions. This allows the Resistance to challenge the world superpower on even terms.

The Resistance fleet primarily serves for coastal defense and convoy raiding. For these purposes, Alligators with Caiman support, as well as hunting packs of Barracuda submarines, fit well.

The Resistance Air Force is one of its strengths. The Hawk strike fighter jet is perfectly suited for a variety of tactical objectives and is able to hold its own in dogfights. The Resistance, unlike the Confederation, also uses attack helicopters in its military.

![](https://i.ibb.co/Jwt1Bsc8/tur-nautilus-polishing-B-alt.jpg)

## Nuclear Weapons

> ...We must take possession of nuclear weapons to win this war...

![](https://i.ibb.co/GvVjKgCB/Tur-nuke-polishing-pravki-B-1.jpg)

During global rearmament at the beginning of 2030's, the Confederation has also rescinded its nuclear arsenal. The majority of the nuclear weapons have been destroyed, but the warheads in Libya have remained conserved in underground bunkers. It is difficult to say what caused this - a simple bureaucratic mistake, Senate's plans for potential future use, or actions of those unhappy with its policy.

During the new world war, information about these bunkers ended up in the hands of the Resistance. Soon enough, despite the Confederation's attempts to stop the rebels, the nuclear warheads themselves were also captured. Now the organization has some truly terrifying weaponry, and tactical nuclear weapons find active use on the battlefield.

It is known that the Resistance was planning to perform an act of terror, striking Confederation cities with ballistic missiles. Nuclear-armed submarines were planned to be used for this purpose.

![](https://i.ibb.co/rGgQ57J6/w-02.jpg)

![](https://i.ibb.co/KpwVBwNn/event-syndicate-standart.jpg)

When the Global Confederation firmly established its power in 2018, it seemed that a new era of stability was just around the corner. However, not everyone benefited. The military-industrial complex was hit the hardest: the Confederation cut military budgets and defense contractors shut down production. Thousands of engineers and workers found themselves unemployed.

Some adapted to the new rules. But many refused to accept their fate.

![](https://i.ibb.co/0VZLjDdg/tour-syndicate.jpg)

## Birth of the Syndicate

In the shadow of the glittering future the Confederation promised, a secret group of former defense industry magnates emerged. For them, global peace meant financial ruin. Thus, the Syndicate was born — an organization driven by a far greater goal than merely regaining wealth and status. They wanted war. Perpetual war.

Large sums of money, moved covertly, fueled an aggressive technological race. While the Confederation made unprecedented scientific strides, the Syndicate still outpaced them by years. The turning point came with the discovery of a new element — Uranum. By purchasing all facilities capable of mining and processing it, the Syndicate created a series of breakthrough technologies that remained hidden from the rest of the world.

It was at this time that a legendary figure arose within the group: John Doe. His cold, calculated logic, sharp insight, and commanding presence enabled him to rise to the top, with no rivals left standing.

![](https://i.ibb.co/wZVW9xp0/blitz-duel-syndicate.jpg)

## The Situation in 2040

Twenty years have passed. A global economic crisis developed due to growing social inequality — an issue the Confederation failed to address. This was at least in part a result of the Syndicate's machinations. It secretly lobbied favorable legislation in the Senate while sponsoring Resistance movements, cultivating pockets of instability.

By 2040, the Syndicate's influence had infiltrated every layer of society — from ministerial offices to underground rebel workshops to the high command of the Confederation. Both sides of the war became dependent on its arms, data, and technology. Each faction was promised victory, but the conflict only dragged on.

Neither the Confederation nor the Resistance welcomes this uncomfortable alliance — but both must accept it, for rejecting it would give the other side a decisive technological edge.

![](https://i.ibb.co/ynrg6b4L/event-syndicate2025-standart.jpg)

## A Secret Empire

The Syndicate blends the structure of a corporate entity with the mystery of a secret order. John Doe fiercely protects his plans, even from his closest associates, revealing only what each unit needs to know.

Agents mask their identities under codenames, and many lead double lives — as public-facing corporate managers, scientists, or officials. Their neighbors would be none the wiser that the friendly face next door is part of a secret organization — or that they themselves are working for it via shell foundations, political parties, and companies.

![](https://i.ibb.co/qMwk6tJp/skirmish-syndicate-f2.jpg)

## On the Cutting Edge of Progress

Advanced data encryption technologies enable the Syndicate to control the global information flow. While investing in various scientific fields, it particularly favors two over others: autonomous combat systems and cybernetic implants. Prototype war machines, piloted by artificial intelligence, are already appearing on the battlefield.

Rumours paint an even darker picture. Some conspiracy theories claim the war itself was fomented, at least in part, to create more injured veterans — future clients for implants. Terrifying as it is to consider, only John Doe knows how much of this is true.

![](https://i.ibb.co/MxVRBGvb/event-syndicate-standart-Doe.png)

## The Syndicate’s “Godfather”

Officially, John Doe is “first among equals”. Yet everyone who encounters him knows his power is nearly absolute. He controls Uranum extraction and processing, commands assets larger than state budgets, and manipulates people so masterfully that even the strongest-willed become pawns.

With age, he’s had more and more cybernetic implants replace his weakening flesh. However, make no mistake — his mind remains ruthlessly cunning and fearsomely dangerous.

Thus, the Syndicate continues to weave its web of intrigues, turning the world into their chessboard. And while some fight for freedom and justice and others — for order and progress, only John Doe truly knows what’s really at stake in this war.

lore.title: New Year Traditions
lore.lead: How people in the world of Art of War 3 preserve holidays during wartime.
lore.body:
In 2040, the war between the Confederation and the Resistance has engulfed almost the entire world. In these difficult times, holidays have taken on special significance: they help people escape daily anxiety and, at least for a short while, feel connected to their loved ones.

## Day of Hope

![](https://i.ibb.co/tp6nvdF8/promo-9years-25-me6.jpg)

Soon after the formation of the Global Confederation, a new holiday was announced — the Day of Hope. It is celebrated annually on January 1, immediately after the New Year festivities. This is a universal holiday meant to unite the planet’s inhabitants regardless of nationality, culture, or religious beliefs. On this day, cities of the Confederation are decorated with symbols of progress and harmony: installations with the flags of member states are set up in city squares, and large-scale light shows fill the sky.

The main tradition of the Day of Hope became the "Dream Exchange". People leave their goals and expectations on special holographic stands or in digital capsules. These messages are then collected and archived, forming an annual repository of humanity’s hopes.

With the outbreak of the global war, the holiday changed. The Day of Hope became not only a symbol of the future, but also a reminder of the fragility of peace. Parades appeared, showcasing humanitarian equipment and rescue drones, as well as "Moments of Remembrance", when residents gather in central squares to honor the fallen.

Over time, the Day of Hope turned into an important cultural institution of the Confederation — a reminder of the value of progress, freedom, democracy, and human solidarity.

## Holidays of the Resistance

![](https://i.ibb.co/HfdsB4K0/NY-24-promo-1.jpg)

In many regions of the world, the Day of Hope never truly took root. After the rise of the Resistance, it was not formally banned, but in practice it came to be perceived as a symbol of the Confederation’s ideology. For residents of liberated cities and rural areas, this holiday was associated not with hope, but with promises that were never fulfilled.

Gradually, local holidays and traditions began to return in its place. Many of them acquired a new meaning — a symbol of liberation from the power of the Confederation and the Senate. At the same time, the Resistance never developed a single alternative holiday capable of replacing the Day of Hope.

This difference became fundamental. Where the Confederation strove for universality and a shared symbol of the future, the Resistance accepted diversity and fragmentation as the norm. In people’s minds, the idea took hold that hope cannot be established by decree, and that it does not have to be tied to a single specific date.

## The Evergreen Crisis

![](https://i.ibb.co/Myc3FGH8/tour-header-28.jpg)

Nevertheless, the New Year continues to be celebrated all over the world — including in Resistance-controlled regions. And, as before, fir trees are needed for the celebration. Due to unresolved environmental issues and population growth, a shortage of coniferous trees emerged over time. With the outbreak of war, the situation only worsened, and providing trees for the holidays became a separate challenge for both the Confederation and the Resistance.

However, humanity recognizes the need to treat the problem of fir trees seriously. Both the Resistance and the Confederation relocate some trees to special reserves where they are protected, and actively plant seeds of new conifer species. In this way, people strive to preserve the tradition of New Year celebrations and pass its joy on to the children of the future.

lore.title: 2038. The Peruvian Conflict
lore.lead: The background of the conflict that became a global war.
lore.body:
## Background

![](https://i.ibb.co/b5x8xDcv/w-04-1.jpg)

In 2018, shortly after the end of the war between the North Atlantic Coalition and the Great Asian Alliance, the World Confederation was formed. The new global government managed to temporarily put an end to interethnic conflicts and redirect the freed military budget resources toward accelerated technological progress.

Over the following twenty years, humanity achieved significant advances across many fields of science and technology. The overall standard of living rose noticeably. However, technological breakthroughs failed to resolve one of the most persistent problems — social inequality. Tensions continued to build, and by 2038 the Confederation faced its first armed uprisings, initially in the Middle East and later in South America.

## Peacekeeping Mission

![](https://i.ibb.co/j9Xc7g2B/blitz-blitzcrieg.jpg)

The uprising spread across several major cities, including Pucallpa and Huánuco, but the Confederation Senate underestimated its scale. Small peacekeeping units deployed to the region under the command of General William Norman encountered fierce resistance within the very first days of the operation.

Despite only limited success in the vicinity of Pucallpa, unit captain Steve Rogers managed to identify the leader of the uprising — a man named Miguel Monteros.

At General Norman’s insistence, Senator Heinrich Seiler, who was responsible for the operation, ordered several reconnaissance satellites to be redeployed from the Middle East to the region. The satellite images forced the Confederation’s leadership to urgently revise its priorities: additional forces and resources were sent to Peru.

Soon after, the peacekeeping corps began inflicting serious defeats on the rebels near Huánuco. Thanks to General Norman’s capable command, the support of his adjutant Natalie Jannet, and Captain Rogers’ tactical ingenuity, a major rebel base was destroyed. During the operation, the Confederation captured Miguel Monteros along with several other leaders of the uprising. The remaining forces were forced to retreat into the mountains and jungles.

It seemed that the region had finally come under the Confederation’s control.

## The Army of Liberation of Peru

![](https://i.ibb.co/PvmXDYPJ/blitz-change-unit.jpg)

However, Miguel’s brother, General José Monteros, had no intention of surrendering. Over the next three months, he methodically gathered scattered rebel units, uniting them into the Army of Liberation of Peru.

At the same time, the Confederation significantly strengthened its positions in the region, making the rebels’ situation even more difficult. Nevertheless, General Monteros devised a bold plan. By splitting his forces, he launched a series of diversionary attacks and maneuvers, forcing the Confederation to redeploy troops, personnel, and supplies along vulnerable routes.

That was exactly what he wanted. Army of Liberation ambushes set up in the jungles and mountain passes intercepted and destroyed a large portion of Confederation convoys. As a result, the peacekeepers lost bases and positions that had previously been considered impregnable.

Exploiting the growing chaos, José Monteros ordered his officers — Colonel Andrés Rodríguez, Major Álvaro Melgar, and Captain Alejo Martínez — to launch a full-scale offensive from two directions. During the fighting, the rebels managed to seize Confederation encryption codes and intercept their radio communications, dealing another serious blow to the peacekeeping forces.

In a final attempt to hold the region, the Confederation command concentrated all remaining troops in Peru’s capital, Lima. However, after a brutal assault, the city was ultimately taken. In a public address, General José Monteros announced the creation of the independent Republic of Peru and called for the beginning of a world revolution.

Soon afterward, major uprisings erupted in other countries across South America, Africa, Asia, and even Europe. Disparate liberation and revolutionary movements united under the single banner of the Resistance — and the local conflict turned into a global war.

lore.title: The Heist of the Century
lore.lead: Resistance fighters raid a Confederation base for valuable Cryocapsules.
lore.body:
Silence hung heavy in the dark interrogation room, broken only by the impatient tapping of a stylus belonging to the investigator in a blue uniform of the Confederation Security Service. Across the table sat a soldier in dirty, bloodstained clothing. He looked defeated, his face covered in bruises and scars.

“So, tell me again exactly how you came upon the decision to steal Cryocapsules from the ‘Kairouan’ military base?” asked the investigator, pressing the record button.

The man across from him let out a raspy chuckle.

“It all started at the poker table back at our base and a poorly timed joke about General Hartman… who just so happened to be walking by. We got stuck serving patrol duty as punishment, our Coyote got cooked in this damn heat, slid into a ditch, and flipped. I remember crawling out onto the road, looking back — and yelling at the top of my lungs…”

“…So how the hell do we explain this now?! Miguel, did you not check the cooling sensors before we left? Was it the vodka?”

“Hey, you were drinking with the rest of us! We all got in the car together…”

“Silence!” barked Sergeant Myers.

Even at night, the heat was unbearable. Grunting and panting from the sweltering air, the soldiers climbed onto the road, activated their personal armor cooling systems, and looked around.

“And anyway, Sergeant, we’re here because of your blabbering mouth. No one forced you to run it…” Miguel Santos muttered under his breath.

“Private Santos is making a valid point,” snapped the Japanese sniper wrapped in a ghillie cloak. The patch on his armor read “Yamamoto A.”

The sergeant thoughtfully turned a radio over in his hands. At that moment, a strange noise behind the hill caught his attention. A glow shimmered in the darkness, and the sound grew louder.

“Confederates,” hissed Miguel. The group dashed for the trees, activating the Infantry Scouting boost. They had just enough time to hide when a Cyclone appeared over the hill. The helicopter circled their overturned Coyote, scoured its wreckage with a spotlight — and flew off. The sergeant’s eyes followed it, and he was grinning like a predator.

“I’ve got an idea for how to get out of this mess…”

The man across the table fell silent. The investigator kept writing. Noticing the pause, he looked up.

“Well?”

“What?”

“How did you get the Cyclone to land?”

“Trade secret.”

The sergeant laughed hoarsely. The investigator liked his sense of humor no more than General Hartman had.

“Listen. We don’t have time to waste. Keep your mouth shut, and you’ll get to hang out with my colleagues again. Who knows what might happen while I’m gone…”

There really were guards waiting outside. The sergeant already got to know them a bit more intimately than he liked, just before this interview. He glanced at the watch on the investigator’s wrist. A change of subject was in order.

“Analog? In this day and age? Swiss?”

“I prefer the classics. Automation isn’t always reliable,” the investigator replied irritably.

“Well, the Cyclone’s pilot clearly didn’t agree. Yamamoto’s one of our best snipers. Took out the scanners with a single shot. The pilot thought they got fried from the heat and landed. Then Miguel and I… and voila.”

“Where is the body?”

“The body? Come on, we didn’t kill him. We tied him up and left him under the trees. Even figured out how to turn on the cooling system in his suit. Hope he didn’t get the wrong idea about us sticking our hands in there, hehe. And after that…”

…The Cyclone approached the Confederation base beyond the hill. The spotlights swept the surroundings. The cockpit, clearly not built for three, was barely holding in the air.

“So what now? Sergeant?”

“Shut up, Miguel. I trust Yamamoto at the controls more than I trust you. Over there — those are cooling towers. Next to them, a warehouse. That’s where the Cryocapsules are. We grab them, and when we get back to base, they’ll give us medals instead of punishment.”

“That’s a great plan, Myers, that’s ingenious, if I understand it correctly. Like a Swiss watch,” Yamamoto replied, with the slightest bit of sarcasm shining through the cracks of his stoic demeanor, as he brought the chopper down.

But just before landing, static crackled in the headset.

“Flight 6-16, do you copy? This is Control. We’re seeing unusual data. Confirm status. Over.”

Yamamoto pressed the transmitter.

“Control, this is 6-16. Sensors are glitching. Requesting maintenance on arrival. Over.”

Tense silence followed.

“Acknowledged, 6-16. Landing authorized. Out.”

“Yamamoto, how do you know how to talk to the Confederates?”

“Saw it in a movie. They always talk fancy like that.”

The Cyclone slowly descended onto the landing pad…

“…And then we sneaked into the warehouses while you guys tried to figure out what was wrong with the Cyclone. Funny how there were barely any guards in the way — we sent them off to dreamland. When we got to loading the capsules, you all finally caught on and sounded the alarm…”

“Damn it, damn it! Miguel, secure the last one!”

The sergeant rushed to the gate control panel and slammed his fist on the button. But just as the gates started to open, a squad of Assaults stormed in from the other side of the warehouse. They spread out and opened fire. Yamamoto, behind the wheel of the truck, exchanged a look with the sergeant and floored it. Miguel, standing in the cargo hold, lost his balance and fell beside the capsules.

Myers, cursing, ducked behind a column and returned fire. He couldn’t even stick his head out. Pulling an EMP grenade from his belt, he aptly threw it right at the enemy’s feet. A dull “whoomp” sound boomed, and their weapons went silent — giving the sergeant just enough time to break out of the warehouse… and come face to face with a flamethrower’s muzzle. Myers noticed the soldier’s jump pack was still cooling from landing.

“Looks like your buddies ditched you, terrorist. Surrender.”

The voice was distorted through the helmet. The sergeant hesitated — then dropped his rifle.

…Myers fell silent. The investigator finished writing, sighed, and turned off the recorder.

“Listen… We both know this is crap, right? You three just waltzed into the base? ‘Took out the scanners’? ‘Saw it in a movie’? ‘Sneaked into the warehouses’?”

The sergeant smirked, without looking at the investigator. The latter continued:

“Myers, our bases are full of cameras. Digital locks. Patrols. You really think I believe this? You’ve been feeding me this load for four hours. Your pals ran. Are you really willing to rot in prison for them — and that’s the best-case scenario?”

The sergeant lifted his head. Their eyes met. The investigator thought he saw a flicker of surrender in Myers’ gaze. He switched the recorder back on. The sergeant looked to the side, as if listening for something, then smiled and spoke:

“There’s one more thing. We had help. A man named… named… Sugon…”

The investigator walked over and leaned closer, trying to hear better.

“What?”

“Sugon… Deez…”

“WHO?!”

Myers suddenly looked up and roared with a wide triumphant grin:

“SUGON DEEZ, YOU CONFEDERATE FILTH!”

And then came a loud explosion. The wall behind the investigator collapsed. Alarms howled across the base. The door to the interrogation room burst open and two guards rushed in, but — bang, bang! — two clean shots took them out.

Yamamoto stepped through the breach in the wall, wrapped in his usual sniper’s cloak. Stepping over the unconscious investigator, he effortlessly picked the handcuffs with a lockpick — as if he practiced every day.

“Excellent work, Sergeant. You masterfully bought us the time we needed, as always.”

Sergeant Myers, rubbing his wrists, looked down at the investigator. Then, he snatched the Swiss watch from him and turned it around thoughtfully in his hand.

“I could’ve stalled even longer. These guards are like kindergarteners. In Zurich, after that bank job, they beat me for an hour and a half before the search…”

The fighters laughed as they exited through the breach, where Miguel was already waiting with a grenade launcher. A few more explosions thundered nearby. The Jaguars on the hill clearly weren’t planning to stop now.

“Surrender! You’re surrounded!” a voice blared from a relay. A squad of Assaults appeared in their path. The sergeant looked at Yamamoto. The sniper silently handed him a rifle…

lore.title: Silver Wings
lore.lead: Brave Confederation aces face a new threat.
lore.body:
The roar of ion engines tore through the sky. Two Vertex fighters, gleaming in the silver-blue colors of the Confederation, flew high above Nevada.

— "Hermes", do you copy?

— Roger, "Wanderer", I hear you.

— "Hermes", isn’t it damn boring out here?

— "Wanderer", cut it out. We’ll both end up scrubbing the birds back at base for chatter like that. Patrol flights count as combat sorties too, you know.

— Don’t be such a drag, "Hermes". Come on, let’s at least practice some rolls, huh? No one’s around anyway...

"Wanderer", a young guy with a voice like a Hollywood actor, glanced for the thousandth time at the display of his IRS-40 — the tracking and targeting system pilots nicknamed the "intrad". The odds of anything showing up there were slim.

— Fine, "Wanderer". Acknowledged. Preparing for maneuver.

In his cockpit, "Hermes" sighed, shaking his head. As the fighters closed in, he frowned and tapped the instruments.

— "Wanderer", hey! You’re too close. Lost your mind? You want to gamble two machines worth tens of billions each?

— Relax! Don’t you trust me? How many years have we flown together? I was even the frontman at your wedding!

The planes drew within just a couple of meters. "Wanderer" gripped his controls.

— "Hermes", do you copy? Something’s wrong with comms. Lost your signal. You’d better brace yourself — I’m starting!

"Hermes" cursed.

— Come in! "Wanderer", come in! Damn you… I know you can hear me!

The two fighters, so close their advanced electronics started glitching, slowly entered a synchronous spin around their axis, sketching a graceful pirouette in the sky. Tension was high in both cockpits. Adrenaline, along with the g-forces, pressed against their bodies: eyes bulged, hearts pounded into their boots. The roll indicator crept upward: 30, 90, 150, 220, 250, 270...

— Yeeeehaaaaw! Ha-ha-ha! — "Wanderer" finally let it out when the planes pulled out of the maneuver and broke away. — "Hermes", you alive down there? Didn’t crap your pants, did you?

— Roger. Glad your comms are back. Confirm: fuselage intact, pants dry.

A sudden ping from the tracking system cut their laughter short. On their augmented-reality helmets flashed an alert: "Incoming message", and the face of the squadron commander appeared on the HUD.

— Not for long, "Hermes". I just got the telemetry from your Vertices, but I’ll chew you out back at base. "Valkyrie" and "Shadow" have engaged enemy aircraft near your position. Your "intrads" already pulled the data from "Guardian". Support them immediately. Priority is pilot protection, understood? Every person and every machine counts. Out.

— Roger, base. Moving out. Out.

The fighters raced toward the blip marked on their radar.

— "Valkyrie", "Shadow", this is "Wanderer". "Hermes" is with me. We’ve got tangos on the intrads, closing in on their six. Ready to begin joint maneuvering on your signal, code zero-zero-delta-six.

— This is "Valkyrie"! Copy, signal zero-zero-gamma-eight. Get these guys off our backs!

There were five Resistance Hawk heavy fighters. Their dark, hulking silhouettes hounded the pair of Vertices, herding them into a trap. One latched onto "Shadow’s" tail again, but the nimble fighter slipped free with a neat loop. "Valkyrie", with a masterful turn, dodged a burst from an autocannon at the last moment.

— "Hermes", I’ll cover "Valkyrie"! Take "Shadow"!

— Got it, go!

The two pilots split in the sky, diving onto the Resistance heavies. A salvo of their Storms sent two burning Hawks down — their pilots barely managed to eject. "Valkyrie" and "Shadow", seizing the confusion, shook off their pursuers, and the four Vertices regrouped.

— Nice work! — came "Valkyrie’s" voice. — So, afterburners on and back to base? Those rust buckets can’t keep up anyway.

— Yeah, time to head home. "Wanderer"? "Wanderer"! Come in! Damn, what now?..

"Wanderer’s" plane broke formation, diving toward the regrouping Hawks.

— If we hit them now, none will make it back to base! We outnumber them, and they’re mid-turn!

"Hermes" swung his fighter around. "Valkyrie" fell in behind him.

— "Wanderer", "Hermes", are you insane?! — "Shadow" shouted over the radio.

But his fighter dove into the attack as well. Four Vertices once more pounced on the Hawks. Two more enemies, trailing smoke, spiraled downward. The last one popped flares, yanked into a loop, and latched onto "Shadow’s" tail...

— Fast little devil! How did he pull that off? I’m locked! I’m locked!..

In "Shadow’s" cockpit, the missile lock warning shrieked. Without wasting a second, "Wanderer" switched his fighter into VTOL mode.

The Vertex’s engines roared like a beast as they swung downward. The fighter tumbled forward, and "Wanderer" switched it back into interceptor mode. Now inverted, the craft dropped, then surged with speed again. His temples throbbed, ears rang. Every fraction of a second counted. He threw his whole body against the stick, forcing the plane to "dive down" — which, in that position, meant "up."

It was enough. The Hawk was dead ahead. The "intrad" locked on, and two missiles streaked from under the wings. But the enemy had already loosed one of his own…

One Storm sharply altered course and slammed into the enemy missile, while the second tore through the opponent’s wing. The Hawk spiraled downward in flames and vanished.

— Mission complete. All targets neutralized. Returning to base.

"Wanderer" and "Hermes" shifted uneasily outside the squadron office, whispering to each other. A female voice from inside called:

 — Enter!

Behind the commander’s desk sat a strikingly beautiful woman in the uniform of a Confederation captain. She slammed her palm against the report.

— Jonathan "Wanderer" Stout… Anton "Hermes" Reznik… Very, very pretty synchronized barrel roll, I won’t deny it. Five Hawks downed… But Major Stanley gave a direct order to prioritize saving lives! Every pilot counts, your fighters cost tens of billions, and this isn’t an air show!

The pilots, caught off guard, stiffened at attention. The captain rose sharply, hands clasped behind her back, and nodded.

— At ease. I am Captain Henrietta Scholz, your new squadron commander. Major Stanley has briefed me on your records and given me his personal assessment of your conduct.

She swept her gaze over them, her calm voice edged with steel by her German accent:

— Lieutenant Stout. Lieutenant Reznik. Stunts like that will not fly with me. Disobey orders again, and I’ll see to it you never take to the skies again. Understood?

— Yes, ma’am!

For a split second, the captain smiled.

— Good boys. Now get out of my office. The Confederation will need your squadron soon.

— Ma’am, permission to speak?

Henrietta raised a brow at "Wanderer."

— Granted, Lieutenant Stout.

— Why isn’t Major Stanley commanding us anymore?

— That’s none of your concern, Lieutenant.

— Ma’am, with all due respect…

— Lieutenant. I advise you to stay out of it. I wouldn’t be surprised if Command’s decision had something to do with your antics.

Silence fell. "Wanderer" stared boldly into the captain’s eyes. Finally, he forced out:

— Yes, ma’am. Permission to leave?

Scholz only waved her hand. The pilots hurried out. The captain sat back down and buried herself in the dossier, though she couldn’t shake her thoughts of the defiant lieutenant. That boy is a powder keg…

Two days later…

— Ladies and gentlemen, welcome aboard our aircraft. The outside temperature is damn hot, because we’re in Nevada. We’ll be at the Mexican border in no time. Please turn off your electronics, phones, and laptops, and fasten your seatbelts…

— "Wanderer", clear comms.

A squad of four Vertices sliced the air, flying low over the desert. The machines wavered slightly, trying to keep formation. On their augmented-reality visors, pilots saw all readouts projected before their eyes — along with the cold face of Captain Scholz.

— The enemy has deployed four next-generation Falcon reconnaissance drones with stealth systems in this region. Their design is based on Chameleon technology.

A projection of a triangular drone flared on the visor, captioned: “Falcon, UAV.”

— The intel came from Security Service military intelligence, not from “Guardian”. “Guardian” cannot detect these drones. They’re moving in from the south. We cannot allow them to locate the base. Your mission is to sweep the sector, find, and destroy the Falcons. Rely on optics, not your intrads. Understood?

— Yes, ma’am!

— Aye!

— Copy!

— Good. Commence operation. Out.

Her face and the projection blinked away. The pilots were left alone with the sky.

— Squadron, spread out! — "Wanderer" ordered.

The fighters widened their spacing.

— "Hermes", anyone see anything?

— Negative, "Wanderer."

— No contacts.

— Same here… Wait…

— What is it, "Shadow"?

"Shadow" squinted into the distance.

— Looks like… some kind of odd cloud.

As they closed in, the squadron spotted a Falcon cloaked in a swirl of masking particles. "Valkyrie," moving in for the intercept, manually fired a missile. Guiding it by optics, she struck true: the drone shattered to pieces.

— Target destroyed! One down, three to go.

Within two minutes, the squadron had downed a second recon drone. But the celebration was short-lived.

— Copy, this is Control. “Guardian” has detected incoming enemy aircraft. Looks like they realized the element of surprise is gone and dispatched Hawks to escort the remaining drones. Be careful. Priority is destroying the Falcons. Out.

The third drone was destroyed before the intrads picked up the interceptors. Four Hawks were on an intercept course.

— Confirm tango presence. Shadow, Wanderer — find the last drone. Valkyrie and I will handle the guests.

— Roger that. Wanderer, swing in from the right.

The squadron split: two fighters surged ahead, while the other two climbed to meet the enemy.

Lieutenant Stout stared at his intrad screen with frustration: chasing drones felt like child’s play…

Seconds passed. A minute. The horizon was clear. Where was that damned drone?!

— Valkyrie, get on contact three’s tail. I’ll draw their fire.

— Almost… got it! Damn thing’s weaving, can’t get a lock!

Shadow and Wanderer flew in silence, listening to their comrades’ comms. At last Wanderer snapped:

— They can’t handle it! Shadow, I’m going in!

— Stop, Wanderer! We need to find the last drone. If it spots the base, we’re in serious trouble. Are you here to do your duty — or just prove how cool you are?

Wanderer’s grip on the stick tightened. His nerves were at the breaking point.

— Valkyrie, target down, confirmed. Hermes, break!

— I can’t shake him off my tail!

— Careful! They’re boxing you in!

— It’s fine… fine…

Wanderer hesitated. Duty. The mission. But his friend was right there — and in mortal danger. The choice was made: Shadow could hunt the machine, he would protect his comrade!

His Vertex rolled hard into a sharp turn.

— Wanderer! Get back here! We have a mission! — Shadow’s shout dissolved into static.

— Hermes, you’re locked! I’m on his six…

— I’ve got it, Valkyrie. I’ll manage…

Reznik maneuvered desperately, trying to delay the inevitable. But it couldn’t last forever. The onboard computer shrieked — launch was imminent. Hermes released flares… and then two explosions thundered behind him. The warning tone cut off — along with the pursuer’s signal.

— Hermes, I got him.

— Wanderer?!

— Clear comms. We still have two tangos.

The three of them swiftly finished off the remaining enemies.

— This is Shadow. Last drone destroyed.

— Excellent! Another successful mission!

Wanderer smirked under his helmet: once again, he’d been right. But then the captain’s face appeared on the visor. Scholz looked… disappointed.

— This is Control. Confirming the destruction of the Falcons… but you were too late.

His heart sank. What?!

— Control, repeat. What do you mean?

— The enemy managed to locate the airbase. Command has ordered evacuation. But Guardian reports large groups of aircraft inbound — and a Leviathan-class signal. They’ll arrive before we can pull out. Return for refueling — you’ll be needed for the next sortie.

The flight back was silent.

The fighters touched down, and the pilots stepped onto the tarmac. Chaos met them. Engineers and base personnel scrambled to prepare defenses and evacuation. Everything portable was packed and loaded onto transports.

Captain Scholz approached. Her usually steel expression was somehow even colder.

— Your fighters will be refueled and rearmed. Lieutenant Stout — you are grounded from combat sorties.

— What?! You can’t do this! If I hadn’t turned back, Lieutenant Reznik wouldn’t be standing here!

— I can. And I already have. The decision is confirmed by Command. Pack your things. Your case will go before the flight commission.

— My case?! How dare you…

Scholz locked eyes with Wanderer. For an instant, he thought he saw… regret? But aloud she said:

— One more word, Lieutenant, and you’ll be under arrest. Understood?

— Yes, ma’am.

As she walked away, she fought to keep her composure, hiding her true feelings. Her heart twisted, but orders had to be followed — no matter how good the pilot, no matter how much she… liked him.

Lieutenant Stout mindlessly shuffled things in his quarters when a knock came.

— Come in… Hermes? What are you doing here?

— I… wanted to say thank you.

— You’re welcome. Anything else?

Wanderer was on edge, no outlet for his anger and despair.

— Actually, yes. Look, I get that this is hard on you…

— Anton, the sky is my life! This isn’t just hard. That frigid witch thinks she’s above everyone? What makes her deserve Stanley’s place? My father flew with him, and now she’s going to give me orders?!

— Johnny, listen. If you don’t follow orders, you’ll never fly again.

— To hell with orders! Would you rather have died up there?

— I could’ve ejected! Sure, we’d have lost one fighter. And now? Thanks to you, we might lose everything!

— Actually, Shadow could’ve found that damn drone faster! My fault? Or that coward’s? Probably stalling — scared some tin can in a cloud would shoot him down!

— Johnny!..

— You know what, Anton? Get out. You’ll do just fine without me, won’t you?

Hermes left without a word, slamming the door.

The massive flying fortress Leviathan loomed over the airbase. The colossus’s guns poured the Resistance’s fury onto airfields, supply centers, the headquarters and the power plants. Squadrons of Hawks swarmed around it, clashing with the Vertices scrambled in alarm.

— I’m hit!

— Flanking!

— Two on my tail, need support!

— Careful, Leviathan’s AA is active!

A pair of Vertices charged the fortress itself, but their Storm missiles lost lock as the Leviathan spewed out a cloud of flares. Ammunition wasted.

Wanderer, standing at the headquarters window, watched the battle raging in the skies. His friends were out there.

Most of the personnel had already evacuated. Only he, the base commander, and a handful of comms officers remained. There was still a chance of victory — but fighters were falling one by one. Shadow, Valkyrie, Anton… all risking their lives.

When the Leviathan deployed flares again, Stout suddenly felt an idea crawl into his mind. He knew how to force the cruiser to retreat. He glanced at Captain Scholz… but there was no time to explain. To hell with permission — he was the only one who knew what had to be done.

His Vertex waited on an empty pad. The pilot slipped toward the machine; it was still fueled and armed.

— Lieutenant, where do you think you’re going?

The voice behind him made him flinch. He turned.

— I want to know what you’re doing here.

— Captain Scholz. I’m going to take my fighter up, ma’am.

— Who authorized this?

— No one, ma’am. It’s my decision.

She studied him closely. Once again, he couldn’t help but note how devilishly beautiful this cold, hard woman was.

— In that case, return to headquarters and await evacuation.

— Negative, ma’am. I will take off.

— Excuse me?..

— The lives of our pilots — my friends — are in danger. I know how to bring down the Leviathan.

He paused.

— Please. Trust me.

Silence stretched between them. Henrietta stepped closer… then suddenly gave him a deep kiss.

— Wanderer, takeoff granted. And I order you… come back alive. Just dare disobey me.

She watched his fighter lift into the sky.

Maneuvering deftly, Stout’s fighter quickly climbed.

— This is Wanderer, copy! I know how to scare off the big hen. I need support. Who can join me?

Hermes was first to answer.

— Wanderer?! Damn am I glad to hear your voice! Shadow, cover Valkyrie. I’ll back our hotshot with his crazy plan!

— Roger!

Hermes’s fighter slid up alongside Wanderer’s. Just like the old days, Stout thought.

— The idea’s simple as a bullet. The Leviathan only triggers flares against massed missile strikes. But a single fighter? They don’t bother!

— Got it, Wanderer.

— Ha, all these years together weren’t for nothing!

— Get ready to dump your whole payload at once…

The fighters closed to within a few meters. Wanderer gripped the controls tight, sweat rolling down his forehead.

— Commence maneuver!

The two fighters, so close their advanced electronics started glitching, slowly entered a synchronous spin around their axis, sketching a graceful pirouette in the sky. Tension was high in both cockpits. Adrenaline, along with the g-forces, pressed against their bodies: eyes bulged, hearts pounded into their boots. The roll indicator crept upward: 30, 90, 150, 220, 250, 270...

The plan had to work. It must. Completing the maneuver barely a meter apart, the fighters straightened on course for the Leviathan.

— Fire!

Two full salvos launched in unison. Before the Leviathan realized it wasn’t just one attacker, the missiles slammed into its hull and engines, rocking the giant. The colossus shuddered… but held.

The pilots watched.

— That hurt it… but next time the flares will come.

— And we can’t delay. Their repair systems will kick in…

Tension coiled. Then, suddenly, Wanderer’s fighter dove straight at the Leviathan.

— Wanderer! Where are you going?! You’re out of ammo! Hey!

— Sorry, Hermes. Comm’s acting up… can’t hear you on the channel.

Henrietta’s face flashed in his mind. He smirked under the helmet.

— Forgive me, Captain. Looks like I’ll have to disobey one more order. My last.

His fighter slammed at full speed into the Leviathan’s smoking engine. The explosion lit the sky. The giant pitched — and this time it couldn’t recover. With a thunderous crash it broke apart, falling in fire and debris. The remaining Hawks scattered in retreat.

Victory. But at what cost?..

Captain Scholz, pale and weary, raised her eyes to Hermes standing in her office.

— Lieutenant, I believe I dismissed you. Debrief is over.

— Uh… Yes, ma’am.

Her gaze softened for a moment.

— Reznik. This is war. In war, there are losses. Remember that. Remember Stout, when you take to the skies again.

Behind her words of encouragement, pain lurked — but Reznik couldn’t know.

— Understood, ma’am…

Hermes left. He wandered the hall in a daze, until the chatter of two young pilots reached him.

— They say he hated following orders!

— So what?

— So he was so good they still took him on sorties. Couldn’t fly without him!

— I don’t know… Seems to me there’s no room for ego in war.

— That wasn’t ego. That was heroism!

On the wall, among portraits of the fallen, hung a fresh one: Jonathan "Wanderer" Stout. Hermes stepped closer.

— Did you fly with him? — one of the young pilots asked.

Hermes looked at him. Then smiled.

— Yes. And I’ll never have a better leader.

lore.title: Dead Frequency
lore.lead: Heroes from earlier stories meet amid an alien zombie invasion.
lore.body:
A magpie flew over an autumn hill. It was not disturbed — nor could it be — by the scattered hulks of smoldering war machines, the numerous explosion craters, or the groans of wounded and dying soldiers.

The bird landed on the ground beside one of the fighters. Its attention was caught by something shiny hanging from his neck. The magpie tugged at the chain with its beak — but the trinket stubbornly refused to come loose. After hopping around for a while, it finally gave up, grabbed a spent shell casing — well, that was shiny too — and carried it off to its poplar tree. Slipping into the hollow, it carefully placed the find near the entrance to decorate its home.

But a growing rumble made the bird peek outside — and that alone saved it from the fireball that suddenly crashed into the tree. With a deafening roar, a heap of burning metal destroyed in a split second everything the magpie had worked on for weeks…

…And minutes earlier, Anton “Hermes” Reznik, in the cockpit of his jet fighter, was desperately trying to regain control while the systems screamed at him with every possible alarm:

— Warning! Critical damage to the fuel supply system. Land immediately. Warning! Automatic wing stabilization system failure. Warning!..

Another explosion shook the aircraft violently, and “Hermes” involuntarily let out a grunt. The still somehow functioning “intrad” — the IRS-40 intelligent tracking and targeting system — showed that unidentified flying objects were still relentlessly pursuing him, unleashing wave after wave of either laser beams or plasma bolts.

— Come in, base, this is “Hermes”! Mayday, mayday, I’m going down! Ejecting!..

He yanked off the safety and pulled the lever sharply. The cockpit canopy blew off, and the seat shot upward. The round “flying saucers” sped after the burning, increasingly bright wreck of the fighter, while the pilot watched it go. The “Vertex” crashed into the trees at the edge of the hill. The UFOs circled the burning pines for a moment, then vanished without a trace.

In the sudden minutes of respite, as Anton slowly descended by parachute, he had time to think over what had happened.

The sortie was going to be just like any other. He, “Shadow,” and “Valkyrie” had been assigned a tactical task: provide air support for a ground operation in the region. They expended their ordnance on the designated targets — and then, out of nowhere, these strange objects appeared and opened fire on the aircraft. “Shadow” and “Valkyrie” managed to shake their tails, but “Hermes,” it seemed, had not been so lucky.

Well, so be it. He could only hope his comrades made it back to base safe and sound.

His thoughts drifted again to a long-dead comrade. If “Wanderer” had been in his place… he would surely have outwitted the intruders with ease and destroyed the UFOs!

The parachute slowed his descent — but not enough to make the landing soft. Anton hit the ground with his legs, fell, rolled several times, and quickly began cutting himself free from the folds of fabric with a knife. Getting to his feet, he was about to survey the battlefield he had landed on, but a voice from behind cut his thoughts short:

— Drop the knife, kid, and hands behind your head. No funny business.

“Hermes” decided not to play hero and calmly followed the instructions.

— Turn around. Slowly.

The voice, as it turned out, belonged to a man in a Resistance sergeant’s uniform. There were three armed men in total — the speaker with an assault rifle, a sniper beside him, either Japanese or Chinese, and another soldier with a grenade launcher, his face hidden under a helmet.

— Well, well, looks like you bit off more than you could chew, huh? Yamamoto, cover me, I’ll search him — could have a tracker or something…

After the search, the Resistance fighters relaxed a little.

— Name and rank, pilot.

— Anton Reznik, Senior Lieutenant, Confederate Air Force.

— Well yeah, you’re not the top brass of a kindergarten. Care to explain what the hell’s going on? Where did these flying saucers come from? Why are they shooting at both you and us?!

— Myers, hey, maybe we shouldn’t babysit him? Just leave him for the corpses to chew on and be done with it… — groaned the grenadier from under his helmet.

— I’ll leave your dumb ass! He’s too valuable — can’t you see, a whole lieutenant. Yeah, a confederate, but we can trade him for our pilots later.

— Speaking of the “corpses” Private Santos mentioned, — the sniper said crisply, with an accent. — I see movement in the scope. Six hundred fifty meters, southwest.

Reznik involuntarily turned to where the sniper was looking. Something really was moving there — as if someone were trying to crawl out from beneath the wreckage of destroyed equipment.

The sergeant grabbed the pilot by the collar of his suit and hissed:

— Not a sound, got it? And don’t you dare piss yourself — these things can smell it from a mile away…

Anton felt the cold barrel of an assault rifle against his neck. The group slowly moved away from the hill. The movement was getting closer, and Reznik could make out its source — a group of humanoids who had once, undoubtedly, been human. Their skin had turned green and hung in tatters, exposing joints, muscles, and bone. Otherworldly, vicious rattles came from their throats, their eyes spinning wildly in their sockets. The remnants of uniforms, armor, and helmets were a grim reminder of who these unfortunate beings had been in life.

Gradually retreating toward the edge of the hill with the others, “Hermes” couldn’t help but notice that the monsters were getting closer. It seemed the crash of the fighter had drawn them in — but now they were searching for the group deliberately. One of the creatures suddenly turned toward the four, sniffed the air, and let out a furious screech…

— Run! Move, move, move!..

The Resistance fighters bolted, fleeing down the hill, and Anton followed suit. There was the sound of a Boost activation — the infantry seemed to grow wings. They moved faster and faster, leaving the pilot behind.

Anton ran as hard as he could until he lost sight of his captors. He was driven forward by the screeching and roaring of the ever-growing number of horrific monsters closing in behind him.

He ran and ran, trying not to look back. Breathing became harder and harder. His legs felt like lead. His knees screamed, reminding him of the recent landing. His gear seemed ten times heavier. Something hit his back — then came a sharp pain. Falling, he rolled onto his back and saw one of the creatures, snarling and drooling, raising its claw above his head…

Bang! A loud shot rang out, and at the same instant the zombie’s head burst apart, scattering in pieces. Several more shots followed, then a burst of automatic fire.

— Hey, lieutenant, come on, don’t just lie there!

Reznik turned toward the voice. In the doorway of a small house stood the sergeant — Myers, he thought — firing into the crowd of advancing zombies with his rifle. From the window of the same cottage, the sniper methodically blew the creatures’ heads off one by one. The pilot gathered what strength he had left, got to his feet, and through the pain barely managed to make it.

The sergeant helped him stumble over the threshold. Through the window, Reznik saw silhouettes of “flying saucers” in the sky. They were appearing one after another, as if they had been tracking them the entire time, directing the zombies here.

— We won’t escape! Even “Vertexes” can’t outrun them! — “Hermes” looked around and saw a hatch in the floor. — Move, all of you, into the basement, now! Follow me!

The Resistance sergeant hesitated, but Yamamoto nodded:

— I’ll cover. Santos, you’re up. Sergeant, trust me — and the lieutenant.

The sergeant grimaced, then practically shoved Reznik down the hatch. “Hermes” managed to see the grenade launcher soldier step into the doorway and fire somewhere off to the side, muttering:

— Have fun with this, you bastards!..

The grenade flew off with a loud beeping sound, drawing the zombies after it. One by one, the fighters jumped into the basement, and the sergeant shut the hatch behind them. The cacophony above reached its peak, then came the dull thump of an explosion — and silence.

And only then, catching their breath, did the fighters realize that the “basement” they had dropped into was in fact a technical corridor. Gleaming steel panels, neon lighting, advanced ventilation.

The private whistled:

— Damn… now that’s something. Wish I had a basement like this back at the ranch — perfect for storing crops…

Unable to contain their curiosity, the group spread out, exploring the place they had found themselves in. An eerie silence hung in the air. Only emergency lighting was active, and from somewhere deep within the corridors came strange rustling and rasping sounds.

Anton reached out to open a door — but the sergeant sharply struck his hand with the butt of his rifle.

— Hey, confederate, what, you think just because we saved your hide you can go poking around wherever you like?

“Hermes” blinked in surprise and replied:

— Sergeant, what’s gotten into you? Where exactly do you think I’m going to run? Above us we’ve got bloodthirsty zombies straight out of a Hollywood action flick, and down here I don’t see any sign saying “Exit”!

The sergeant clearly hadn’t expected pushback. His cheeks flushed, and he swung as if to strike again — this time at the face — but Yamamoto firmly grabbed his arm.

— Sergeant Myers. There is no need to worry. I am watching the pilot closely and will not let him escape.

For a fraction of a second, the fighters stared into each other’s eyes — Myers’ filled with rage, Yamamoto’s with cold restraint. At last, the sergeant lowered his weapon, yanked his arm free, and opened the door himself.

The room they entered was some kind of vast storage facility. Rows of machinery lined the shelves.

It was freezing cold. Anton shivered involuntarily. Private Santos said in a surprised voice:

— Sergeant, look. Aren’t these some kind of computers — like the ones the techs bolt onto our vehicles?

Yamamoto, Myers, and Reznik stepped closer.

— I don’t know, Miguel, I’m not a technician. Yamamoto, ever seen anything like this?

— Looks like targeting systems for weapons. We mount those on our equipment.

“Hermes” turned his head and looked over another rack in surprise.

— IRS-40? Who would need an entire rack of “intrads”?..

And then, behind the shelving, the pilot saw a human body in a ballistic vest lying face down. Judging by the scattered shell casings, he had died fighting for his life. His weapon — a large-caliber pistol — lay beneath the corpse. Reznik took advantage of the Resistance fighters being distracted, pried the pistol loose, and slipped it into an inner pocket of his flight suit. Lucky — there were even a couple spare magazines on the body’s belt.

Now all that remained was to wait for the right moment to escape. Sadly, his personal communicator had been destroyed in the crash.

Moving on, they entered a small office. On the desk lay some kind of device in a disassembled state. Nearby was a desktop computer. Yamamoto stepped closer and sat down in the chair.

— I don’t know what to do. Two-layer protection. The first one seems simple — a standard Resistance cipher. But beyond that…

“Hermes” could see what came next. A memetic blocker used to protect Confederate systems. Anton took a step toward the sniper to help, but Myers moved to block his path, raising his rifle.

— Nope. Where do you think you’re going? Not happening. You’ll probably activate some robots to kill us.

— So what, we’re just going to sit here and wait while Yamamoto spends a hundred years cracking a cipher I see every day?

— What if we do? At least I trust Yamamoto. You’re a confederate. Why would I trust you? I know your methods. Your two-faced nature! Your habit of betraying people at the first opportunity. The way you recruit fools like me into assault units, promising them the world — and when they die, you don’t even bother to bury them…

Once again, tension hung thick between Reznik and Myers. The pilot opened his mouth to respond — but Santos suddenly shouted:

— Guys, we’ve got problems! A lot!..

And then came the roaring and screeching of the infected drawing closer. The sergeant turned his attention away — and Reznik didn’t hesitate. He lunged for the computer. Shoving the startled Yamamoto aside, he quickly entered an override command into the memetic cipher, and data flooded the screen — tables, graphs, schematics. “Hermes” couldn’t believe what he was seeing. Someone here had been researching the possibility of transmitting signals on a frequency undetectable by modern instruments.

— And here, looks like evacuation schematics, — Yamamoto said flatly. — I’ll upload them to my visor.

— We need to get out of here! I don’t think the locals appreciate our visit! — Santos thundered, bursting into the office. Turning around, he fired his grenade launcher down the corridor. An explosion echoed through the halls, followed by the sickening, wet sound of zombie flesh being torn apart.

Meanwhile, with a furious shout, the sergeant lunged at the pilot. Reznik barely managed to dodge the incoming rifle butt — it smashed full-force into the monitor instead. The screen couldn’t withstand the blow, bursting apart with a pop, scattering sparks and shards of plastic.

— Myers! Snap out of it!.. They’re going to tear us apart!

— You think you can give me orders, confederate? I’ll blow your brains out…

The sergeant knocked Reznik to the ground. “Hermes” reached for the hidden pistol — but at that moment Santos slammed into Myers. Rolling over, the sturdy grenadier pinned the sergeant firmly to the floor.

— Myers, come on — can you please, for just two minutes, hide your boner for beating up the confederate?

— Fine, fine… we’ll settle this later. For now — move!

The private nodded, got to his feet, and signaled Yamamoto, who was already working the corridor with his sniper rifle. The squad moved out, careful not to get surrounded. Sergeant Myers called out to the sniper:

— Hey, Yamamoto, where are we going?

— According to the floor plans, there’s a large elevator nearby. We’ll get to the surface — should come out close to our base.

After dealing with several more infected, the group reached the elevator. It was a large cargo platform stacked with crates, in the center of a vast chamber — the heart of the underground base. At the middle of the platform stood a massive metal container, shaped like a drop pod or a strange pyramid with its top cut off.

“Hermes” couldn’t shake the feeling that he had seen something like it before.

The sergeant strode decisively toward the control panel while the others climbed onto the platform. Lowering his rifle, he began pressing buttons, trying to activate the lift — but out of the corner of his eye, he caught sight of Reznik raising a heavy pistol that had seemingly appeared out of nowhere…

— I knew it!.. — Myers managed to shout, raising his weapon, before “Hermes” fired. Once. Then again. And again.

The smell of gunpowder. The sound of a throat choking on blood. The dull thud of a body hitting the ground.

To Myers’ surprise — not his own. Breathing heavily, he stared wide-eyed for a couple of seconds at the smoking barrel of the pistol in Anton’s hands, then turned and saw a zombie corpse lying right at his feet.

— Thanks, — the sergeant muttered under his breath, then returned to the control panel. The elevator came to life. The platform slowly began to rise, and the chamber filled with the thunder of machinery and the snarling of zombies drawn by the gunfire and the moving lift.

The squad fired back, cutting down the infected trying to climb onto the platform. With every shot from Yamamoto, another head burst apart. Myers emptied magazine after magazine into the pressing horde. Reznik fired his pistol, and between reloads smashed enemies with the grip and kicked them away with his heavy boots. Santos laughed wildly as he mowed down zombies in groups.

At last, the platform rose high enough to nearly reach the ceiling. It obligingly split apart, letting the fighters see the light of the setting sun once more.

The first thing they heard was the air raid siren from the nearby Resistance base. Then came the annoying high-pitched firing sound of the UFOs, which were surrounding the base and striking it again and again. Defensive structures were barely holding back the endless stream of zombies.

On the horizon, where “Hermes’” airbase was, flashes were also visible. Reznik realized his comrades were in danger too.

The platform rising from underground had clearly attracted attention — not just from the zombies, but from the UFOs as well…

— Those s-saucers… are they controlling these things?.. — Santos stammered in fear.

— Faster, we need to get out of here! — Myers shouted.

But suddenly, Reznik had a realization. He remembered what the strange metal container in the center of the platform resembled. Rushing to it, he began feeling along its edges and seams, searching for a small recess which, according to the schematics from the computer, would open a sliding control panel.

— Buy me five minutes. Please!

— Are you insane? If you’re planning to die here, I’m not going into the grave with you! — Myers shouted back.

Reznik looked him straight in the eyes.

— Myers, I know I’m asking a lot. Just… trust me. This base might hold the key to our survival. All of us.

In a split second, Sergeant Myers weighed what he had heard. A struggle raged inside him. He couldn’t go against his beliefs, he couldn’t… But here and now, he and Reznik were not “Resistance” and “Confederate.” They were simply people. People whose home planet was under invasion.

— Damn it… Yamamoto, Santos — secure the perimeter! Miguel, get all your toys out — mines, traps. Yamamoto, take out the big ones first, leave the small fry to me and the private. Confederate… do what you have to. We’ll cover you!

“Hermes” ran his hands along the container and found the hidden recess. Pulling with all his strength, he tore the panel free and revealed a touch control screen. The display looked suspiciously similar to a familiar IRS-40, but all the text was written in some unknown language made up of dots, dashes, and curved lines. The pilot had to proceed almost blindly, relying on instinct and his experience flying “Vertexes.”

— We can’t hold them for long, kid! Hurry up! — Myers shouted.

— Just… a moment…

Could the entire container be one massive communication device? But how to send a signal… And what kind?.. Reznik launched program after program, but nothing worked.

A zombie, shot mid-leap by one of the defenders, landed with a dull smack right beside Anton.

— There are too many of them! — Santos’ voice rang out.

“Hermes” exhaled. He remembered the day when “Wanderer,” saying his final goodbye, had rammed his “Vertex” into the engines of the “Leviathan.” “Sorry, ‘Hermes’. Comm’s acting up…”

He remembered the feeling of helplessness as he had shouted into the microphone, trying to make his friend abandon that fatal decision…

Now he had a chance to atone — here and now, for the sake of saving others.

— Go. Get out of here! I’ll manage… You’ve done everything you could.

Without waiting for a response, Reznik turned back to the controls — but at that moment, several laser beams struck the platform right beside him. “Hermes” looked up — one of the flying saucers was hovering directly overhead, seemingly having materialized out of thin air. The high-pitched whine of charging laser cannons sounded again…

— HEY! HEY! OVER HERE, YOU BITCH! YOU FILTH! PENDEJO!

It was Santos, who had climbed up onto the crates and was waving his arms. He even fired his grenade launcher upward, but the grenade didn’t make it halfway and exploded off to the side.

Whoosh, whoosh, whoosh! Bursts of alien fire exploded around the grenadier, swallowing him in a cloud of fragments and smoke…

The few seconds bought by the private gave Reznik the time he needed. Finally grasping how the device worked and launching the correct program, he heard a rapidly rising hum from within and felt the mechanism vibrate. With a distinct click, the top of the container opened, and a blinding signal beam shot into the sky. UFOs began appearing one after another — and then…

A miracle happened.

At first, it seemed like nothing had changed. But the UFOs hesitated. Hovering in place, they finally opened fire — not at the humans, but at the zombies. Volley after volley cut the monsters down, reducing them to heaps of ash.

Myers and Reznik shouted in triumph. Even Yamamoto exhaled in relief and smiled, lowering his rifle to take in the sight. The sergeant clapped the pilot on the shoulder — he was still standing by the device, detaching a small data storage unit and slipping it into his pocket — then looked around and shouted:

— Private Santos! Miguel! Come out, we won! Santos?..

Joy turned to tension.

“Hermes” went pale. Once again, someone had sacrificed himself for his sake. No. No… it should have been him!

Then came a rustle. A groan. And finally, from beneath a pile of debris, the grenadier’s hand burst out — fist clenched, thumb raised.

— Y-yes, sir… arghh… boss!..

The sergeant looked at Reznik.

— What’s with the face, confederate? Were you already mourning a fallen Resistance fighter? Remember this, friend — everyone in my squad is ready to face death, but I’m not letting anyone take that final rest ahead of time. Got it?

— Yeah. Got it. Now I got it.

“Hermes’” gaze fell on the “intrad” display mounted on the signal device. Several “blips” were rapidly approaching — signals he was familiar with all the way back at boot camp.

He suddenly stepped back, drawing his pistol and aiming it at the Resistance fighters. Myers and Yamamoto immediately did the same.

— Nothing personal, sergeant. But I swore an oath of loyalty, — Reznik said calmly, slowly backing toward the edge of the platform.

— So did I, confederate. What, you think you’re faster on the draw? You’re going to take us all out with that peashooter?

— No. Of course not.

Reznik turned the pistol and pressed the barrel to his own temple.

— I just know you need me alive. “He’s too valuable.”

Myers laughed.

— Now that’s something!.. Go on, threaten to bomb your own base while you’re at it. One less confederate, one more…

— I’m sure it’ll look great in your report — that you shot a captive. You do write reports in the Resistance too, right?

Yamamoto frowned, staring into the sky.

— Sergeant. We’ve already lost. Look…

There, in the sky, a squadron of “Cyclone” helicopters was rapidly approaching the platform. The sergeant and the pilot exchanged glances. Myers grunted.

— Damn… fine. You win, confederate. Santos, Yamamoto — we’re leaving. Target escaped.

— Wait, sergeant, there aren’t many of them. I could—

— Corporal Yamamoto, that’s an order.

— But—

— Move!

The sniper looked at Reznik, then slowly lowered his rifle and headed toward Santos.

As he left, Myers called over his shoulder:

— You fought well. If we meet again, confederate… I hope you’ll put up a proper fight.

— Likewise, Sergeant Myers.

For a few seconds, Anton watched them go. The silhouettes of the Resistance fighters dissolved into the wreckage and smoke. He slowly lowered his pistol.

Reznik turned and took a step forward — toward his own. He looked at a magpie flying overhead, somewhere toward the poplars.

His hand slipped into his inner pocket. His fingers found the small data storage device. He pulled it out and held it in his palm for a moment.

Cold. Light. Almost weightless. And yet — so heavy.

Anton clenched it tighter and looked up at the sky, where the UFOs still circled, methodically burning away the remaining zombies. Then — toward the Resistance base.

— So that’s how it is… — he exhaled quietly.

The key had been found. Only now, it would have to be used against those he had just fought beside.

lore.title: Gold of the Irish Resistance
lore.lead: The story of Ireland's Resistance Army and the country's hidden gold reserves.
lore.body:
Commanders! Have you read the description of the "Gold Rush" Blitz Tournament? It already hinted at the origin of the gold you're fighting for, and today, we'll tell you the full story.

The creation of the Global Confederation in 2018 sparked unrest in many countries, and Ireland was no exception. Despite its location in Western Europe, the freedom-loving and proud nation viewed the unification with caution, even with official assurances that the national identities of member states would be preserved.

Years passed. Ireland remained part of the Confederation, but its development began to slow. The Senate failed to effectively address growing social and economic inequality. Distrust gradually turned into open discontent, and by 2038, an underground organization had formed: "Arm Fhriotaíochta na hÉireann" — literally, the "Resistance Army of Ireland."

In 2039, with the support of a mysterious benefactor, the organization amassed enough weapons and equipment to launch an uprising. RAI cells simultaneously attacked Confederation garrisons in several major cities. Dublin fell under rebel control, forcing the government to evacuate.

However, by that time, the global war with the Resistance was already escalating, and the Senate responded far more quickly than it had in Peru or the Middle East. In less than a week, reinforcements arrived on the island, and the Irish Resistance forces were forced to retreat.

The rebels abandoned Dublin, but during their withdrawal, they managed to take the country's gold reserves with them. Pursued by Confederation peacekeeping forces, RAI leadership soon realized they would not be able to leave the island with the gold. A decision was made to divide the treasure and hide it in Connacht, in western Ireland. Some equipment and weapons were hidden there as well.

This decision allowed them to preserve what mattered most: their people. The Resistance Army of Ireland managed to evacuate from the island in an organized manner. General José Monteros personally welcomed the fighters, declaring them heroes of the Resistance.

A year later, the Resistance is ready to return to the shores of Éire to reclaim the hidden gold. Meanwhile, the Confederation never stopped searching, and its Security Service has finally provided the Senate with the presumed coordinates of the lost reserves.

Commanders, don't miss your chance to secure victory for your faction in this conflict: collect as many Pots of Gold as possible!

lore.title: Эксперимент
lore.lead: Доктор Камилиус представляет с экрана телестудии блестяще прошедший климатический эксперимент. Но за идеальной математической моделью скрывается цена, которую город заплатил человеческими жизнями.
lore.body:
В студии мягко гудели системы охлаждения, но на лбу доктора Камилиуса блестели капли пота. Команда помощников заканчивала последние приготовления к выпуску, проверяя, чтобы ведущая и доктор выглядели безупречно и в кадр не попало ничего лишнего.

Учёный никогда не любил публичные выступления, но что поделать: просьба председателя Академии наук Конфедерации — скорее приказ.

— Двадцать секунд до эфира! Освободите площадку! — раздался голос из динамика. Людей вокруг словно ветром сдуло.

Камеры задвигались по студии. Послышалась музыка вступительного ролика.

— С вами Анджела Парадайз, вы смотрите вечерние новости на канале "Свобода". Лето вновь вступило в свои права, а вместе с ним вернулся и самый острый вопрос сезона: хватит ли Криокапсул всем жителям планеты?

Ведущая говорила чётко и громко — сказывался многолетний опыт работы.

— В ходе Антитеррористической операции Сената Конфедерации пострадал целый ряд заводов корпорации Cryotech. Официальные представители называют ситуацию "контролируемой", однако со всех концов Земли поступают тревожные сообщения: энергосети перегружены, в десятках регионов зафиксированы отключения электричества, а обычные кондиционеры не справляются даже с относительно низкой температурой около пятидесяти градусов, не говоря уже о настоящей жаре.

Девушка повернулась к доктору Камилиусу. Камера плавно сместилась, захватывая в кадр их обоих.

— Сегодня у нас в студии доктор Камилиус, почётный член Академии наук Конфедерации, лауреат Нобелевской премии и куратор климатического проекта в Сан-Антонио, недавно завершившегося крупным успехом. Добрый вечер, доктор.

— Благодарю за приглашение, Анджела.

— Доктор, расскажите подробнее о проекте. Аномальная жара с нами уже не первый год, но инфраструктура и энергосистемы всё ещё не справляются. Как вам удалось преодолеть эти трудности в масштабе целого мегаполиса?

Камилиус слегка расслабился в кресле, стараясь выглядеть естественно.

— Конечно, аномальная жара — одна из главных проблем человечества. Наш совместный эксперимент с Cryotech и Сенатом Конфедерации был призван разработать наиболее эффективную систему распределения Криокапсул в условиях постоянно растущего спроса и возможного дефицита. И эксперимент, можно сказать, прошёл блестяще. От начала и до конца...

---
